Yes, but I don't understand why you're asking that question.

Its an example for when an issue is completed, these are all the payments to all the contributors who helped complete the task. In this example scenario, you received comment incentives on the issue and review. You can click to expand the details.

We will eventually roll out a proper leaderboard once the XP system is implemented. Basically the vision is to have a repo, org, and global XP ranking. The more tasks completed, the higher the XP goes. Then we can introduce task gating, where, for example, an organization can gate off high priority items to bounty hunters with a rank of 100 or more within the repo (or org, or global.)

Overall the code looks pretty solid but I have some concerns.
`-1` would be more explicit to say that there was an error in getting the `userId`? Why should we support `undefined`?
We need to stop relying on `"https://pay.ubq.fi?claim="` but I guess it might make more sense to handle as part of another issue.

Perhaps I jumbled things up with another specification but I wanted it to be configurable in case partners did want to give comment incentives to assignees.

We have another issue where it uses `new URL()` to make sense of it 
The final implementation will rely on comment metadata which is an html comment inside of the bot comment

Unfortunately it's really tedious for me to find the original spec / list from my phone but I want to clarify that there are eight recognized ways to contribute and we should stick with the same terms 
Prefix (which view) this part you got right
1. Issue
2. Review
Role:
1. Assignee
2. Issuer
3. Collaborator -> added to repo, has authority to leave official review states etc
4. Contributor -> everybody else
